claim: Playback of three vervet alarm-call types in the absence of predators elicited different receiver escape or vigilance responses.
context: Free-ranging vervet monkeys; predator absent during playback
methodology: Recorded alarm playback with observed receiver behavior
limitations: Response discrimination is not proof of linguistic semantics or propositional meaning.

claim: Harmonic-radar tracking documented flight paths of honeybee recruits after they followed waggle dances conveying food-source direction and distance.
context: Honeybee foragers and recruits; remote food sources
methodology: Harmonic radar tracking of recruited foragers
limitations: The abstract documents trajectories but does not independently isolate every potential odor or landmark cue.

claim: The authors report context-dependent variation and combinations of rhythm tempo rubato and ornamentation features in sperm-whale codas.
methodology: Computational and statistical structural analysis of codas
limitations: No demonstrated decoding of coda meanings and no playback-based confirmation of semantic function in this study.

claim: The study reports rapid reciprocal gestural exchanges between chimpanzees with quantifiable response latencies.
context: Face-to-face chimpanzee gestures in observed social interactions
methodology: Video-based temporal coding of gesture exchanges
limitations: Comparable timing is not proof that chimpanzees use human linguistic conventions.

claim: Male mourning cuttlefish were reported to use different lateral visual patterns directed at female and male observers in particular courtship settings.
context: Wild courting males with multiple nearby conspecific receivers
methodology: Photographic coding of lateral skin patterning and social configuration
limitations: The article uses the term deception but observer coding alone cannot prove an animal's conscious intent.

claim: Electroantennography and trail bioassays found that tested ant species could detect some other species' pheromones and that Lasius niger followed a mixed trail farther than its own pheromone trail.
context: Synthetic trail pheromones; tested sympatric and allopatric ant species
limitations: Heterospecific following can be eavesdropping and does not prove intended cross-species signaling; results differ by tested ant.

claim: Group-living Calloconophora pinguis nymphs were reported to recruit siblings to new feeding sites using plant-borne vibrations and coordinated group signaling.
context: Sibling groups feeding on newly expanding host-plant leaves
methodology: Field observations and experimental vibrational/behavioral responses
limitations: Group-recruitment results should not be generalized to all treehoppers or insects.

claim: Live Mormyrus rume synchronized electric-organ discharge intervals in some close interactions with conspecifics or a mobile fish robot emitting electric signals.
context: Small groups and an electro-communicating mobile fish robot
methodology: Electric-signal recordings and robot playback manipulation
limitations: Electric-organ discharges also serve electrolocation; social-attention function is partly hypothesized.

claim: Spontaneous sigh breaths were measured in four unrestrained dogs during wakefulness and both REM and NREM sleep.
context: Unrestrained dogs in waking and sleep conditions
methodology: Respiratory volume timing and muscle activity measurements
limitations: No socially available recipient or communicative response was evaluated in this experiment.

claim: The authors report that sigh frequency in rats correlated with relief after a threat-associated laboratory condition.
context: Rats in conditioning conditions with threat and safety periods
methodology: Laboratory timing of sighs relative to aversive-trial context
limitations: The proposed function as an interpersonal safety signal was not demonstrated with receiver experiments.

claim: Observed horse snort rates varied with pasture and housing situations and covaried with recorded behavioral and welfare indicators.
context: Riding-school and naturalistic horse populations with different housing contexts
methodology: Non-invasive sound/event coding and behavioral welfare indicators
limitations: Correlated snort production does not prove positive subjective experience or signal directed to others.

claim: Deep breaths in rats were coordinated with some ultrasonic vocalizations and were associated with changes in call duration and acoustic modulation.
context: Sprague-Dawley rats during social and noxious laboratory contexts
methodology: Synchronized breathing and ultrasonic vocalization recordings
limitations: Respiration can be a motor substrate of sound production without being a separate intentional social message.

claim: In zebra finches familiar contact-call playback produced stronger HVC interneuron responses than unfamiliar call playback and was associated with faster or more consistent vocal responses.
context: Familiar versus unfamiliar conspecific call playbacks
methodology: Behavioral playback plus separate awake head-fixed Neuropixels HVC recordings
limitations: Behavior and neural measures were partly collected in different experimental arrangements; neural response is not word meaning.

claim: The dog study reports context-dependent differences in several physiological and behavioral markers including cortisol and heart-rate variability.
context: Laboratory conditions interpreted by authors as differing valence and arousal
methodology: Physiological assays and cardiac measures with behavioral measures
limitations: Emotion valence/arousal markers are not themselves proof that a dog has intentionally communicated a state to another animal.

claim: In the studied Japanese macaque group gentle tapping of another macaque was often followed by grooming and occurred especially among adult female dyads.
context: Free-ranging Awajishima Japanese macaque social group
methodology: Behavioral observations and comparisons with grooming solicitation
limitations: Group-specific behavior and possible cultural explanation require testing across populations.
